newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks in third record close this week.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks in third record close this week.

text.p: Mexican stocks notched up their third record close of the week after dealers bought market stragglers on cue from favourable economic data.

"The market is on course. Stocks that had lagged the market led the way, in reaction to data that confirm a favourable outlook for 1997," said Gerardo Copca, equity analyst at the Valores Finamex brokerage.
The leading IPC share index ended up 48.31 points, or 1.28 percent, at 3,826.77. Trading volume was moderate at 73.5 million shares traded.
Mexico's Finance Ministry announced midsession that industrial output for 1996 was up 10.7 percent from 1995 levels.
The Finance Ministry also announced Thursday night that total public debt fell as a proportion of GDP to 33.3 percent, from 44 percent at the close of 1995.
Another analyst said falling interest rates and a firmer peso also helped drive share prices to new highs.
"Public finance data were very good and all economic indicators show that foreign investment is still flowing in," said an analyst who asked not to be identified.

Benchmark 48-hour peso contracts closed 2.5 centavos firmer at 7.77 per dollar, while overnight Cetes, or Treasury bill, rates ended below 20 percent for the second day in a row, a level not seen since the December 1994 devaluation crisis.
"The bourse had to rally, as it has become less volatile," the analyst said.
Other traders said although foreign investors did not enter the bourse in such force as on Tuesday and Wednesday, they did help push prices up towards the close.

"They were quiet for most of the day, but towards the close they were seen to buy more and some decided to stay here for the long weekend," one trader said, referring to the fact U.S. markets will be closed on Monday for President's Day.
On the broad market, 110 stocks were traded, of which 70 gained while 22 declined.

Traders said stocks heading the gainers' list did so on a favourable outlook for fourth quarter earnings. Food company Maizoro topped the list, up 32 centavos (4 cents) to 3.62 pesos (47 cents), followed by retail stock Liverpool, up 36 centavos (5 cents) to 7.40 pesos (95 cents).

One notable decliner was media group Televisa, down 3.80 pesos (49 cents) to 100.00 pesos ($12.87). Traders and analysts said the drop reflected concerns over Televisa Chairman Emilio Azcarraga Milmo's health.

A company official told Reuters Azcarraga was merely resting in his Los Angeles home and not seriously ill. The official said the decline in Televisa share prices in recent days was "coincidental with a fall in the price of other Mexican stocks".
